+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
+# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).

+# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
+# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
+# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
+#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
+#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
+#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
+#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
+#
+# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
+# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
+# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
+# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
+#
+# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
+# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
+# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
+# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
+# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
+schema_version: 1
+
+profiles:
+  lean:

+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false

+    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false

+    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false

+    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
+    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
+    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
+    guardrails.input.enabled: false
+    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
+    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
+    structured_handoff.enabled: false
+    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
+  full:
+    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
+    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
+    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true

+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds

+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'

+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi
+  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
+  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  IFS="$old_ifs"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {
+  local -a toks argv
+  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
+  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
+  _hd_mcls=none
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    t="${toks[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
+      case "$t" in
+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
+          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
+          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+          case "$_hd_up" in /dev/null|/dev/stdout|/dev/stderr) continue ;; esac
+          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
+          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
+          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
+          continue ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+    fi
+    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
+  done
+  (( ${#argv[@]} > 0 )) || return
+  a0="${argv[0]}"
+  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"
+  if _bdb_hd_is_interp "$base" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$base"; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  [[ "$a0" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return
+  (( stdout_files <= 1 )) || return
+  for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+    t="${argv[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  done
+  case "$a0" in
+    cat)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
+    tee)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -a|--append|-p) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;
+    echo|printf)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        case "${argv[i]}" in -n|-E) ;; -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    gh)
+      case "${argv[1]:-} ${argv[2]:-}" in
+        "pr comment"|"issue comment") want=" -F --body-file -R --repo |" ;;
+        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          --body-file=-) stdin=1 ;;
+          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+          -*)
+            if [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" $t "* ]]; then
+              i=$((i + 1))
+              [[ ( "$t" == "-F" || "$t" == "--body-file" ) && "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1
+            elif [[ "${want#*|}" != *" $t "* ]]; then
+              _hd_mcls=interpreter; return
+            fi ;;
+          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    git)
+      [[ "${argv[1]:-}" == commit ]] || return
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;
+          --file=-|-F-) stdin=1 ;;
+          -q|--quiet|-s|--signoff|-a|--all|--allow-empty|--allow-empty-message|-v|--verbose|--no-edit|--amend) ;;
+          *) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    br)
+      case "${argv[1]:-}" in create|update) ;; *) return ;; esac
+      for ((i = 2; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    jq|yq)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
+        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
+        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
+    sed)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
+          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
+               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             fi ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    sort)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+          -k*|-t*) ;;
+          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;
+    wc)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    *) return ;;
+  esac
+  _hd_mcls=nonexec
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
+# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
+# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
+_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
+  local l="${1:-}" k last
+  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0

+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
+#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
+# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
+# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
+# =============================================================================
+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
+_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'

+_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
+_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'

+
+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;

+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {

+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {

+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;

+  return 1
+}

+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {

+  n=${#s}

+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then

+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done

+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an

=== heredoc-classifier.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
     3	# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
     4	# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
     5	# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
     6	# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
     7	#
     8	#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
     9	#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
    10	#                                           all have non-executing consumers
    11	#
    12	# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
    13	# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
    14	# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
    15	_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    16	_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    17	if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
    18	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    19	  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
    20	fi
    21	unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
    22	
    23	heredoc_consumer_class() {
    24	  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    25	    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
    26	  else
    27	    printf 'none\n'
    28	  fi
    29	}
    30	
    31	heredoc_nonexec() {
    32	  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
    33	}

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"

    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi

    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];

   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |

   136	        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
   137	        else . end)) as $knobs |
   138	    {

   140	      id: $id,
   141	      profile: $sel.name,
   142	      profile_source: $sel.source,
   143	      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
   144	      profile_keys: $keys,

   162	}
   163	
   164	_loa_pl_write_cache() {

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])

+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3

+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}

+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage

+      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
+      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
+      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
+      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
+        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
+        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
+        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
+      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
+    else
+      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  if (( json )); then
+    jq . <<<"$report"
+  else
+    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
+           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
+  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    local err drc=0
+    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
+    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
+  fi
+  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
+}
+
 case "$sub" in
-  write) cmd_write ;;
-  read)  cmd_read ;;
+  write)  cmd_write ;;
+  read)   cmd_read ;;
+  derive) cmd_derive ;;
+  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
+  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
+  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   *) usage ;;
 esac

+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+

+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. +- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. +# =============================================================================

+# mode {unset, ask, telemetry, deny} × claims {plain, authoritative} × write {app, trust}
+# × sanction {none, run_fresh, run_stale, marker_fresh, marker_stale, override}
+# × cache {fresh, stale, missing, unparseable} (run_* sanctions define the cache themselves)
+# =============================================================================
+
+# $1 mode (unset = no key) $2 claims (plain | authoritative)
+cfg_gate() {
+    : > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    if [[ "$1" != unset || "$2" == authoritative ]]; then
+        printf 'implement_gate:\n' >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ "$1" != unset ]] && printf '  mode: %s\n' "$1" >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ "$2" == authoritative ]] && printf '  claims: authoritative\n' >> "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    fi
+    return 0
+}
+
+# $1 cache: fresh | stale | missing | unparseable | run_fresh | run_stale (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    case "$1" in
+        missing) ;;
+        unparseable) printf '{"state": "RUNNING", \n' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        fresh)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        stale)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_fresh) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_stale) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+    esac

+
+# $1 sanction: none | marker_fresh | marker_stale | override (run_* handled by cache_state); echoes the override value
+marker_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json"

+        marker_fresh) jq -nc '{skill: "implement", sprint: "sprint-256", started_at: (now | floor | todate)}' > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json" ;;

+gate_cell() {
+    if [[ "$2" == authoritative ]]; then

+    else
+        jq -nc --arg p "$1" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"

+                    local cell="mode=$mode claims=$claims write=$wclass sanction=$sanction cache=$cache"
+                    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$cell: exit $status" >&2; return 1; }
+                    want=$(expect_cell "$mode" "$claims" "$wclass" "$sanction" "$cache")
+                    got="$(decision3)"
+                    [ "$got" = "${want%% *}" ] || { echo "$cell: expected ${want%% *}, got $got" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # the write's decision row: the claim row (model_signal), the trust row (state_write) or the gate row
+                    row=$(jq -sr 'map(select(.action != "note" and (.hook == "implement-gate"))) | if length == 1 then "\(.[0].action)/\(.[0].decision)" else "count:\(length)" end' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null) || row="no-rows"
+                    [ "$row" = "${want#* }" ] || { echo "$cell: expected row ${want#* }, got $row" >&2; cat "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # a stale marker logs stale_marker (and never sanctions) whenever the run path did not sanction first
+                    n_note=$(jq -s 'map(select(.decision == "stale_marker")) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    if [[ "$wclass" == app && "$sanction" == marker_stale ]]; then
+                        [ "$n_note" = 1 ] || { echo "$cell: expected one stale_marker row, got $n_note" >&2; return 1; }
+                    else
+                        [ "$n_note" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: unexpected stale_marker row" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                    # every row this gate wrote carries replay: true under LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 (DEC-0167)
+                    n=$(jq -s 'map(select(.replay != true)) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: $n rows without replay: true" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # telemetry prints nothing at all
+                    if [[ "${want#* }" == telemetry/outside_run ]]; then
+                        [[ -z "$output" && -z "$stderr" ]] || { echo "$cell: telemetry printed something" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                done
+            done
+        done
+    done
+}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
# AC-9.1, AC-9.3; SDD D-9.1, D-9.3)
#
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence
# (explicit key > profile > fallback), every profile defines every key,
# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json), unknown profile, the
# mtime-keyed cache, the overrides line, the /loa Profile line, the readers
# that route through loa_knob, and the grep lint for direct reads.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
    : > "$CFG"
}

knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }

@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    for p in standard full; do
        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    done
    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
}

@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
}

@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
    local k want got
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
    [ -z "$output" ]
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
....
    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
}

@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: turbo\n' > "$CFG"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" profile
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "standard" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *'unknown loa.profile "turbo"; using standard'* ]]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source 2>/dev/null)" = "invalid" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria false 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]
    # A non-string profile is unknown too.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: [lean]\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
}

@test "PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "lean" ]
    # Same stamps → served from the cache: a planted value proves the read path.
    jq '.knobs["decisions.surface_at_session_start"].value = "from-cache"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "from-cache" ]
    # A config edit with a new mtime rebuilds.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-02 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "full" ]
    # A profiles.yaml edit rebuilds too.
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    yq -i '.profiles.full["decisions.surface_at_session_start"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    touch -d '2026-01-03 00:00:00' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "false" ]
}

@test "PL-9 a corrupt or foreign cache file is rebuilt, never trusted" {
    mkdir -p "$T/run"
    echo 'not json' > "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
    jq -e '.schema_version == 1' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" >/dev/null
    jq '.id = "other"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.id' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" != "other" ]
}

@test "PL-10 a seam config without a cache seam writes no cache (the repository cache is never touched)" {
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/root/.claude/data"
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    LOA_PROFILE_ROOT="$T/root" run bash "$LIB" knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x
    [ "$output" = "false" ]
    [ ! -e "$T/root/.run/effective-config.json" ]
}

@test "PL-11 overrides lists the explicit profile keys that differ from the profile, sorted" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\ndecisions:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\nstructured_handoff:\n  enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$LIB" overrides
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'guardrails.input.enabled=true\nstructured_handoff.enabled=true')" ]
}

@test "PL-12 a profiles.yaml key that names a floor key is ignored with a WARN" {
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
    yq -i '.profiles.standard["implement_gate.mode"] = "deny" | .profiles.standard["flatline_protocol"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" knob implement_gate.mode ask
    [ "$output" = "ask" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key implement_gate.mode names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key flatline_protocol names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile_keys | index("implement_gate.mode")' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "null" ]
}

@test "PL-13 a malformed key path returns 2 with the fallback and never reaches yq" {
    printf 'a: 1\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$LIB" knob '.a | env' fb
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"fb"* ]]
    run bash "$LIB" knob 'a;b' fb
    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
}

@test "PL-14 the /loa Profile line prints the profile and the explicit overrides" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE
    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')
    [ "$line" = "Profile: lean (explicit overrides: guardrails.input.enabled=true)" ]
    : > "$CFG"
    run --separate-stderr env CACHE_DIR="$T/wscache" LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/srun" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" \
        LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG" timeout 120 bash "$R/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh" --no-stale-check
    line=$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep '^Profile:')
    [ "$line" = "Profile: standard (explicit overrides: none)" ]
}

@test "PL-15 the guardrail readers route through loa_knob (knob on and off)" {
    printf 'guardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh" --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.reason')" = "guardrails disabled in config" ]
    printf 'guardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh" --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.reason')" != "guardrails disabled in config" ]
    printf 'guardrails:\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh" --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous
    [[ "$output" == *"danger level enforcement disabled in config"* ]]
    printf 'guardrails:\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$R/.claude/scripts/danger-level-enforcer.sh" --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous
    [[ "$output" != *"danger level enforcement disabled in config"* ]]
}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

     5	#
     6	# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
     7	# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
     8	# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
     9	# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
    10	# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
    11	# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    18	    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    19	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    20	    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    21	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"

    30	    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    31	    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    32	    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    33	    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    34	    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
    35	}
    36	
    37	# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
    38	checkpoint() {
    39	    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
    40	        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
#
# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
add_team_block() {
    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
PY
}

add_team_row() {
    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
}

gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }

@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {
    run jq '[.constraints[] | select((.id | startswith("C-TEAM")) or any(.layers[]?; .section == "agent_teams_constraints"))] | length' \
        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "0" ]
}

@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {
    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
....
    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {
    add_team_block
    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    # The neighbouring sections survive with one blank line between them.
    grep -qF '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    run grep -c '^## Agent-Network Primitives$' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    [ "$output" = "1" ]
    run diff <(sed -n '/end merge_constraints/,/^## Agent-Network/p' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md") \
             <(printf '%s\n' '<!-- @constraint-generated: end merge_constraints -->' '' '## Agent-Network Primitives')
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "LI-4 pruning is idempotent: a second run leaves the kernel byte-identical" {
    add_team_block
    gen
    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/first.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    cmp "$F/first.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-5 the generator renders the table when the class has rows" {
    add_team_block
    add_team_row
    run gen
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    grep -qxF '| MUST fixture rule | fixture why |' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ! grep -qF 'MUST stale row' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-6 rows without the heading block fail loudly and leave the kernel untouched" {
    add_team_row
    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"Missing markers"*"agent_teams_constraints"* ]]
    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-7 a marker block with foreign text above it is an error, not a silent deletion" {
    add_team_block
    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
s = s.replace("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |", "## Agent Teams\n\nOperator prose that is not a table.\n\n| Rule | Why |")
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
PY
    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"
    run gen
    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
    [[ "$output" == *"no '## Agent Teams' heading directly above its table"* ]]
    cmp "$F/before.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-8 lint-invariants passes the optional-table invariant on the live tree" {
    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash '$LINT' --json"
    echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.message | test("agent_teams_constraints: table presence matches"))' >/dev/null
    ! echo "$output" | jq -e '.results[] | select(.level == "ERROR" and (.message | test("agent_teams")))' >/dev/null
    # The field name is load-bearing: the negative check above is vacuous if
    # the report shape ever renames `level`.
    echo "$output" | jq -e '[.results[] | has("level")] | all' >/dev/null
}

@test "LI-9 the lint self-test (test-lint-invariants.sh) is green" {
    run bash -c "cd '$R' && bash .claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh"
    echo "$output" | tail -3
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {

....
    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
}

@test "LI-3 the generator removes a leftover Agent Teams block when the class is empty" {

    ! grep -q 'agent_teams_constraints' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

    run grep -c '^## Agent-Network Primitives$' "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()

    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"

  [ "$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase + " " + .state' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = "REVIEW RUNNING" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.derived_at // "none"' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json")" = none ]
}

@test "RCD-13 no active cycle or no ledger → exit 4 with a named reason; the cache is untouched" {
  cache RUNNING
  cp "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" "$T/before"
  jq '.active_cycle = null' "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" > "$T/l" && mv "$T/l" "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
  derive --json --write
  [ "$status" -eq 4 ]
  [[ "$stderr" == *"no active cycle"* ]]
  rm "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
  derive --write
  [ "$status" -eq 4 ]
  [[ "$stderr" == *"no readable ledger"* ]]
  cmp "$T/before" "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

@test "RCD-14 write refreshes the derived cache after its own update; an unparseable cache is reported and never rewritten" {
  complete 101; complete 102; complete 103
  cache RUNNING
  run bash "$CK" write --file "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" --sprint sprint-3 --phase AUDIT
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  run jq -r '[.checkpoint.phase, .state, .status, (.derived_at != null)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
  [ "$output" = "AUDIT COMPLETE COMPLETE true" ]
  printf '{"state": "RUNNING",\n' > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
  cp "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" "$T/before"
  derive --json --write
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(dj '.cache')" = unparseable ]
  [ "$(dj '.written')" = false ]
  cmp "$T/before" "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

@test "RCD-15 impl_commit is the newest non-merge commit since the sprint started that touches a path outside the state set; state-only commits are skipped" {
  complete 101
  cache RUNNING
  local impl
  impl=$(git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD)
  printf 'n\n' > "$R/grimoires/loa/NOTES.md"; printf '# c\n' > "$R/CHANGELOG.md"
  git -C "$R" add -A
  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "docs: state only"
  derive --json
  [ "$(dj '.sprints[0].impl_commit')" = "$impl" ]
  # a sprint started in the future has no implementation commit yet
  jq '(.cycles[1].sprints[1].started) = "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"' "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" > "$T/l" && mv "$T/l" "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
  derive --json
  [ "$(dj '.sprints[1].impl_commit')" = null ]
}

@test "RCD-16 the jack-out step in completion-modes.md writes .state (and mirrors .status) on the sprint-plan cache; run-resume derives on drift; the recovery doc reads .state" {
  local cm="$REPO/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/completion-modes.md" hr="$REPO/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md"
  grep -q '^## Jack-out' "$cm"
  sed -n '/^## Jack-out/,/^## /p' "$cm" | grep -qF '.state = "JACKED_OUT" | .status = .state'
  grep -qF 'run-checkpoint.sh derive --json' "$hr"
  grep -qF 'derive --write' "$hr"
  grep -qF '.reset_at = $ts' "$hr"
  grep -q 'Read `.state`' "$hr"
}

@test "RCD-17 a ledger row without local_label or timestamps keeps its fields aligned (empty TSV fields do not collapse)" {

}

@test "RCD-9 breaker recompute: two -r1 feedback files and a zeroed breaker give cycle_count 2, same_issue 2, no_progress 1; counters are raised, never lowered" {
  complete 101
  feedback 102 review CHANGES_REQUIRED sprint-102 1 1 2026-06-01T01:00:00Z

  cache RUNNING
  printf '{"state":"CLOSED","triggers":{"same_issue":{"count":0,"threshold":3,"last_hash":null},"no_progress":{"count":0,"threshold":5},"cycle_count":{"current":0,"limit":20},"timeout":{"started":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z","limit_hours":8}},"history":[]}\n' > "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
  derive --json
  [ "$(dj '.active_sprint')" = sprint-102 ]
  [ "$(dj '.breaker.recomputed | [.cycle_count, .same_issue, .no_progress] | map(tostring) | join(" ")')" = "2 2 1" ]
  derive --write
  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.no_progress.count, (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 2 2 1 32" ]
  # the recorded hash is the run-mode same-issue hash of the last round
  local want
  want=$(bash "$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-102/auditor-sprint-feedback-r1.md" --gate audit --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)

  derive --write
  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json")" = 7 ]
  # /run-resume --reset-ice stamps reset_at: rounds before it no longer count
  jq '.triggers.cycle_count.current = 0 | .triggers.same_issue.count = 0 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 | .reset_at = "2026-06-01T01:30:00Z"' "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json" > "$T/b" && mv "$T/b" "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
  derive --write
  [ "$(jq -r '.triggers.cycle_count.current' "$R/.run/circuit-breaker.json")" = 1 ]
}

  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi
    done

  # Phase 3: Diff or commit

    for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do

    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    trap - EXIT
    return 0
  fi

  # Commit with rollback
  declare -A backup_files
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local bak="${target}.constraint-bak"
    cp "$target" "$bak"
    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"
  done

  local commit_failed=false
  local committed=()
