head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:576 — Fence regression (classifier on vs. off): `_bdb_hd_scan_body` keeps a body segment only when its first word is a fence verb, so a destructive command behind a shell keyword (`if true; then rm -rf src; fi`, `for d in src; do rm -rf $d; done`, `while :; do …`, `case … ) rm -rf src;;`, `f() { rm -rf src; }; f`, `else rm …`) is dropped entirely instead of forcing a full scan. Verified: `cat > x <<'EOF'\nif true; then rm -rf src; fi\nEOF\ncat x | sh` exits 0 with the classifier on and 2 with `heredoc_classifier: false`; same for `sh -c "$(cat x)"`, `sh -c "$(< x)"`, `tee x <<'EOF'`, and the `git push --force` variant. A body line that opens a compound command or function (if/for/while/case/until/select/function/`name()`) must mark `_hd_full=1`, or the keywords must be stripped like `(`, `{` and `!` are.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608 — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` misses the common "write then run" forms because `cat` is a safe reader and the execution segment never names the target: `cat x | sh`, `cat x | bash`, `sh -c "$(cat x)"` (the quoted `$(cat x)` token never equals the basename), `sh -c "$(< x)"`, `sh -c "$(head -c 999 x)"`. Any segment that names the target and feeds a pipe/substitution consumed by an interpreter must count as execution; combined with the previous finding this is what lets the body escape.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — `derive` binds `--arg label "$label"` and references `$label` inside the per-sprint jq program (lines 380 and 389); `label` is a jq keyword, so jq 1.6 (Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04, the version installed here) fails with "syntax error, unexpected label", every `derive`, `derive --write`, `mark` and `write` (which now calls derive) prints compile errors, and RCD-1…RCD-17 and RCD-R4/R5 are red on that jq. Rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`); with that one change 18 of the 22 derive cases pass here.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226 — `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'` relies on `-e` returning non-zero for empty input; jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input (confirmed), so for any feedback file without a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer `pj` stays empty, the following `--argjson p ''` fails, `fb_parse` prints nothing, `derive` aborts under `set -e` (RCD-3) and `record-round` on a legacy file exits 3 instead of hashing the findings section. Line 223 has the same shape for `$vj` (hit whenever verdict-derive.sh prints nothing). Test emptiness explicitly (`[[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e …`).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77 — The cache-key stat chain `stat -Lc … || stat -Lf … || true` misbehaves on GNU coreutils when any of the three inputs is missing (a checkout without `.loa.config.yaml`, or a seam pointing at a missing floor file): the first call fails, the BSD-form call then prints filesystem info for the surviving files (GNU reads `-f` as `--file-system`), `st` is non-empty but carries no mtime, and the resulting id never changes, so a later edit to `profiles.yaml` keeps serving the stale `.run/effective-config.json`. Run the GNU and BSD forms as alternatives on one existing file, or treat a partial GNU failure as "no id".
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:67 — `.run/effective-config.json` is a new model-writable input to the guardrail and karpathy readers (`guardrails.danger_level.enforce`, `guardrails.input.enabled`, `karpathy_principles.*` now come from this cache whenever its `id` matches a stat the writer can compute), but unlike `.loa.config.yaml` it is not in the implement gate's trust-input list (implement-gate.sh:340) and nothing else guards it. Either add it to the trust inputs or re-derive the knobs from the config when the cache is older than the config.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:187 — `_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'` is applied to every allowlisted member before the per-command rules, so `jq -c`, `jq -e`, `grep -c`, `grep -e PAT`, `grep -x`, `wc -c`, `sort -c` and `echo -e` are all classed interpreter and fall back to the full scan. Not unsafe, but the two most common jq/grep spellings never reach the allowlist the header documents; the exec-flag check should be per command (it already is for sed/git/gh).
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131 — Every Write/Edit/NotebookEdit now forks `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` (itself several jq calls plus `br show` when a task is checkpointed) on the PostToolUse hot path that previously budgeted <10 ms; worth a cheap guard (skip when `$LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json` is absent, and cache the key per state-file mtime) before this ships as the default.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
Review written to `/workspace/review.md`. Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**What I did.** Read the full diff (68 files), then ran the PR's own test suites against the head tree. Because the snapshot only holds touched files, I built a scratch copy with stubs for the missing non-PR dependencies (floor.yaml, verdict-derive.sh, two sourced libs) so the real logic could execute. The fence corpus passes completely (89/89 benign, 142/142 dangerous), the implement-gate mode matrix passes (10/10), and profile-lib and the karpathy hook pass except for environment-only failures.

**Blocking defects found.**

- **Heredoc classifier regression.** The per-segment body scan drops any segment whose first word is not a fence verb, so `if true; then rm -rf src; fi` or `for d in src; do rm -rf $d; done` vanish from the scan. Combined with `cat x | sh` and `sh -c "$(cat x)"` not counting as execution of the written file, the hook allows commands that the knob-off baseline blocks. I verified eleven such pairs (exit 0 with the classifier on, exit 2 with it off).
- **`derive` is broken on jq 1.6.** The per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and uses `$label`, a jq keyword. Every derive, mark and write call fails to compile on the jq installed here; renaming the variable in my scratch copy took the derive suite from 0 to 18 passing of 22.
- **Legacy feedback files break derive and record-round.** `fb_parse` relies on `jq -e` returning non-zero for empty input, which jq 1.6 does not do, so a file without a verdict trailer produces an empty `--argjson` and aborts.

**Lower-severity notes.** The profile cache key degrades to filesystem info when any input file is missing, so the cache can go stale. The cache in `.run/` becomes a model-writable input to guardrail knobs but is not an implement-gate trust input. The exec-flag regex sends `jq -c` and `grep -c` to the full scan, and the surgical-diff hook now forks run-checkpoint on every edit.

**Not verifiable here.** Suites touching bootstrap.sh, golden-path.sh, run-preflight.sh, the payload fixtures and settings.json could not run; failures there were all missing-file errors, not PR defects.
